issues.actual: Repository idiom (CLAUDE.md Layout section) states the Molt/ lean_lib exists precisely so that 'every paper2 Lean citation resolves here', via paper-named definitions with rfl/pointwise bridges to the MoltPetit.Model originals. This is not aspirational: paper/molt.tex:163 and :780 already cite `badKeyrot_lossOnly`/`badSched_lossOnly` by name, and those are Molt namespace theorems living in Molt/Rotation.lean:230,239 (guarded in Molt/Axioms.lean:27-34), not MoltPetit.Model theorems, even though MoltPetit.Model has its own loss-only lemmas the Molt ones bridge to. W6's design breaks this pattern: it edits paper/molt.tex to cite two theorem names that only exist in MoltPetit.Model, with no Molt/ wrapper, no Molt.lean import touch, and no Molt/Axioms.lean-style guard planned or budgeted.
issues.fix: Add a thin Molt/ companion (e.g. Molt/KeyStealingTimedScope.lean or fold into Molt/Rotation.lean) re-exporting/wrapping the two witnesses under the Molt namespace with their own #guard_msgs entries in a new Molt/Axioms* guard file (mirroring badKeyrot_lossOnly/badSched_lossOnly's own pattern), add the two matching import lines to Molt.lean (a second additive root-import touch, same permitted class as the existing MoltPetit.lean touch), and cite the Molt-qualified names from paper/molt.tex instead of the bare MoltPetit.Model names. This adds roughly 20-40 lines and one more touches_existing entry; it does not change the design's core finding or its 'no positive derivation' conclusion.

issues.claim: Implicit in depends_on/enables symmetry: no cross-check is made against sibling design W5.json, which itself declares (in its own `enables` list, key W6) that landing W5 first would hand W6 reusable vocabulary and structure -- specifically a mint-side twin of NoPrematureTheftLock (`NoPrematureMintLock`) plus W5's non-inductive per-window pinning theorem `lockstep_window_declares_rosterGen` -- for W6's 'mode-3 no-back-dating derivation'.
issues.actual: W5.json's enables-entry for W6 (lines ~595-597 of W5.json) is written against a POSITIVE per-mode derivation that this W6 design explicitly and correctly refutes as infeasible under the additive-only constraint (see hypothesis_verdict/recommendation/alternatives_rejected #1-#3 in W6.json). W6.json's own depends_on/enables correctly do not reference W5 at all (no entry either direction), and the two new theorems' reuse lists (verified against source: badSched at KeyStealingSchedule.lean:124, producerForSlot at Definitions.lean:50, badKeyrotOn at KeyStealing.lean:47, inForce/confirmedPrefix at KeyRotation.lean:49/42, keyFloor at KeyIndex.lean:77 -- all line numbers match exactly) touch only pre-existing, timeless MoltPetit.Model definitions, none of them W5- or W3a-introduced. So W6 as designed is genuinely independent of W5 and does not need W5's NoPrematureMintLock/pinning theorem. But W5's own enables-entry is now stale/orphaned relative to what W6 actually delivers -- a cross-design inconsistency between two sibling 'final' designs that a planner merging both should reconcile (either strike or footnote W5's enables-W6 entry, or note it describes a follow-on item beyond W6's current scope, not W6 itself).
issues.fix: Not a defect in W6.json itself (which is internally consistent and does not claim to consume W5's future structure). Record in the planner's cross-design notes that W5's enables→W6 entry should be marked stale/conditional-on-a-future-item once W6 lands with the negative finding, so a later reader of W5.json alone is not misled into expecting W6 to have built NoPrematureMintLock.

issues.claim: Multiple sibling designs (W3a, W5, and this W6) each independently plan to insert their new-module import line(s) into MoltPetit.lean at the identical anchor point ('after import MoltPetit.Model.KeyStealingScheduleTimed, before import MoltPetit.Model.KeyRotationTests').
issues.actual: Confirmed: W3a.json, W5.json, and W6.json all target that exact same two-line gap (verified by grep across all three designs' touches_existing text). This is not a semantic conflict -- import lines are order-insensitive for Lean's purposes -- but it does mean whichever of the three lands first will shift the anchor comment for the next two, so each subsequent design's 'after X, before Y' description needs re-reading against the file as it then stands rather than assumed.
issues.fix: No design change needed. Flag for the integrator: apply these three root-import edits as separate small commits/diffs rather than trying to hand-apply all three designs' MoltPetit.lean patches verbatim in one shot, since the literal 'before/after' text in each design will only match the file's state before any of the siblings have landed.

ordering_notes: W6 as designed is genuinely additive-only and independent: it introduces two new files (one Model file, one Results guard file), touches only the MoltPetit.lean root import list, defines no new structure that any other of the seven items also defines (no loop risk -- grepped all seven sibling design JSONs for KeyStealingTimedScope, NoPrematureMintLock, and both new theorem names; only W5.json even mentions NoPrematureMintLock, as a name for future work it does not itself create, and only W6.json creates the two witness theorems), and reuses only pre-existing, timeless MoltPetit.Model definitions that predate this whole rollout. The stated depends_on (soft, non-hard, on W3a) is correctly non-binding and is explicitly argued down to 'not a real dependency' in the design body -- verified true by the reuse list, which never touches any W3a-introduced file (KeyStealingTimed.lean, SyncRuleTimed.lean, or their axiom guards). enables is correctly empty. The one real cross-item wrinkle is that sibling design W5.json's own enables-entry describes a positive mode-3 derivation route through W6 that this W6 design explicitly and correctly abandons as infeasible under the additive-only constraint -- W6 does not need redoing if W5 lands first or vice versa, but W5's text about what W6 will hand it becomes stale once W6 lands with its negative finding, and a planner reconciling both documents should note that explicitly rather than treat it as still-live. Root-import anchor contention with W3a/W5 (three designs inserting at the same MoltPetit.lean gap) is real but purely textual/sequencing, not semantic. The one substantive layout-idiom gap is the missing Molt/ wrapper for the two new theorems that paper/molt.tex ends up citing by name -- confirmed against two live counterexamples in the same file (badKeyrot_lossOnly/badSched_lossOnly, which are Molt-namespace theorems in Molt/Rotation.lean, not MoltPetit.Model ones) showing the citation convention is enforced today, not merely documented aspirationally.
